cases.title: Added HandleContext to re-enter soft-rewritten Requests. (#709)
cases.bug: HandleContext resets the context (handlers and index) and re-enters routing without restoring them, so the original chain continues on the new route's handlers and middleware re-runs; it also returns c to the pool while still in use

matched.title: reset() mid-handler wipes Keys and index but not the response writer state
matched.failure: A middleware sets Keys (for example an auth user) and then calls HandleContext. The re-entered handlers lose those Keys. When control returns to the outer Next loop, c.index and c.handlers describe the inner chain, so remaining outer handlers can be skipped or run against the wrong chain. If headers were already written, the re-entered route's status is not applied.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading did not confirm the failing case (Re-entering a rewritten request is meant to reset the context and run the new route's chain, so clearing Keys and replacing handlers and index is the design. The outer chain ends once the inner chain finishes, which is what re-entry intends. The writermem state is not cleared, but that is not a bug )

Middleware does not run on direct .fetch calls. A fetch that throws rejects or throws synchronously instead of becoming an error Response.
notes: severity lowered from warn to inform: a second reading did not confirm the failing case (The new test asserts `eventHandler.fetch` is the user's fetch, so keeping the object's own `fetch` is the deliberate behaviour of universal `{ fetch }` handlers.)
